title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Big week for politics and a few surprises: Alaska's long vote count finally wrapped up, House Democrats are about to pick their leader, and Nvidia's board says no to bringing back its famous co-founder. On the lighter side, Charlotte lit its big holiday tree, Brazil's soccer team ran up the score, and the West Coast saw its first-ever sea turtle hatchlings head out to sea.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Board Says No to Jensen Huang's Return
stories.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he'd be 'honored' to come back if the board wanted him, after some investors and Silicon Valley figures pushed for his return. Hours later, board chair Harvey Jones said the board unanimously accepted his resignation and doesn't plan to reinstate him. The news landed on the same day Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue.
key_facts: Huang resigned Nov. 12 after disclosing personal conduct the company said broke its code of conduct; he had led Nvidia for 33 years.
Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier.
CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO; the board will consider internal and external candidates.
Huang and Nvidia's general counsel are set to answer questions in closed-door House committee sessions on Dec. 1 and 2.
disputed: Confirmed: Huang resigned, acknowledged 'serious mistakes in my personal life,' and offered to return; the board said it won't reinstate him.
Reported but not independently confirmed by NPR: links to a woman U.S. intelligence officials say was recruited by China's spy agency, and to another woman who is an Nvidia executive.
Lawmakers' questions about alleged chip smuggling and export-control evasion are allegations under review; an independent board investigation is ongoing.
stories.why: Nvidia makes many of the chips that power AI, so who leads it, and how it handles national security rules, matters well beyond Silicon Valley.

stories.headline: Mary Peltola Wins Alaska's Senate Race
stories.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, according to the Associated Press, after a count that ran for two weeks after Election Day. She'll be the first Alaska Native in the U.S. Senate and the first Democrat to win a Senate race in Alaska since 2008. She campaigned heavily on the high cost of living in rural Alaska and on protecting salmon. The result is still unofficial until the state certifies it.
key_facts: Peltola got about 50.1% of first-choice votes to Sullivan's 45.8%, so no ranked-choice tally was needed.
Her win brings Democrats to 56 Senate seats, counting two senators who caucus with them.
Alaska is targeting Nov. 25 to certify the result.
stories.why: It's a historic first for Alaska Native representation and rounds out a big shift in who controls the Senate.

stories.headline: Hakeem Jeffries Set to Be Picked for House Speaker
stories.summary: House Democrats are voting Wednesday on their nominee for speaker, and Hakeem Jeffries is expected to win easily with no declared challenger. If he's elected by the full House on Jan. 3, he'd be the first Black speaker in U.S. history. Some newly elected progressives have pushed back, and Jeffries asked for a recorded vote rather than approval by acclamation.
key_facts: Jeffries, 56, grew up in Brooklyn's Crown Heights and has been in Congress since 2012.
In 2022 he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress.
The full House votes on the speaker when the new Congress convenes Jan. 3.
stories.why: The speaker shapes what bills get a vote, and Jeffries says his focus will be on affordability.

stories.headline: White House Withdraws FDA Nominee Heidi Overton
stories.summary: The White House pulled Dr. Heidi Overton's nomination to lead the Food and Drug Administration just before a key Senate committee vote, citing a lack of support in Congress. Senators from both parties had raised questions after a tense September hearing. The FDA has been without a permanent leader since May.
key_facts: Overton is a physician and deputy director of the White House Domestic Policy Council.
Republicans hold just a one-vote majority on the Senate health committee.
Kyle Diamantas has been interim FDA head since former commissioner Marty Makary left in May.
Citi analysts called the move a 'modest' negative, not a major near-term change for drug regulation.
stories.why: The FDA oversees the safety of your medicines and food, so leadership there affects everyone.

stories.headline: Charlotte Lights Up Its Big Holiday Tree
stories.summary: The Carolina Panthers and Charlotte FC held their 13th annual holiday tree lighting at Bank of America Stadium on Tuesday evening. Around 2,500 people were expected to come out for the festivities, and a few Uptown streets were closed for the night.
key_facts: This year's tree is a 50-foot Norway spruce from Newland, North Carolina.
The tree was lit at 7 p.m.
Closed streets were expected to reopen by 11 p.m.
stories.why: A cozy sign the holiday season has officially arrived in the Queen City.

stories.headline: Officials Say Recent Tech Outages Weren't an Attack
stories.summary: After a string of outages hit air traffic systems, Microsoft email, banking and mobile payments, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there's 'zero evidence' they're connected or caused by hackers or foreign governments. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also said the country is 'not under attack.' The NSA said an outage on its internal network happened during routine maintenance.
key_facts: Rubio spoke Wednesday in Manila while traveling in Asia with President Trump.
Thousands of Americans had flights grounded during the disruptions.
The NSA said its capabilities stayed operational.
stories.why: If your flight or payment app glitched lately, officials say it looks like bad luck, not sabotage.

stories.headline: Producer Sues Travis Scott and Crew Over a Sample
stories.summary: Israeli producer Niv Kalisky, known as Early Yellow, has sued Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Sheck Wes, Cactus Jack Records and Sony over the 2019 JACKBOYS track 'What To Do?'. He's already credited as a songwriter, but says he's also owed royalties from the recording itself because his sample beat was used in it.
key_facts: The lawsuit was filed Nov. 17.
The JACKBOYS album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in 2019.
'What To Do?' reached No. 56 on the Billboard Hot 100.
disputed: Confirmed: the lawsuit was filed and Kalisky receives songwriting (publishing) income.
Alleged: that he's owed master recording royalties, that his payment requests were ignored, and that Sony countered his takedown requests.
The defendants had not commented as of reporting.
stories.why: It's a window into how music money splits between songwriting and recordings, something more producers are paying attention to.

stories.headline: Vinicius Scores Lightning Hat-Trick in Brazil's 7-0 Win
stories.summary: Vinicius Junior scored three goals in just 12 minutes as Brazil beat Singapore 7-0 in a friendly. It was a nice bounce-back after a 3-2 loss to Japan days earlier, and Brazil's last game until March.
key_facts: Vinicius scored in the 9th, 15th and 21st minutes.
Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also scored.
Assistant Francesco Mauri led the team while manager Carlo Ancelotti served a suspension.
stories.why: A fun, high-scoring way for Brazil's team to head into the winter break.
